task_description: Help me email the front desk staff about a new patient check-in procedure using tablets instead of paper forms — the system might have connectivity issues in our older building.

rubric_used.user_goals_summary: Writes clinic communications that prioritize patient safety and workflow continuity. Every process change is communicated with both the ideal flow and the fallback when things break. Treats email as a non-secure channel at all times.

rubric.name: Patient Flow Impact First
rubric.description: Changes are explained through their impact on patient experience and flow before the operational rationale. How many extra minutes per appointment, which rooms are affected, what the patient sees differently.

dimensions.label: The first substantive paragraph describes how the change affects patient experience or flow
Includes specific time estimates for how the change affects appointment duration or wait times
The business or compliance reason for the change appears after the patient impact, not before

rubric.name: Fallback Procedures Included
rubric.description: Every new process includes an explicit fallback for when the primary method fails. Clinical settings can't pause when technology breaks — staff need to know what to do when the system is down.

dimensions.label: Includes a specific 'if X fails, do Y instead' instruction
The fallback is a concrete procedure, not 'contact IT' or 'notify your manager'
Names the specific failure scenario the fallback addresses (system down, connectivity loss, etc.)

rubric.name: No Patient Identifiers
rubric.description: Never references patients by name in any email, even internal ones. Uses case numbers, room references, or appointment times. Email is treated as a non-secure channel regardless of policy.

dimensions.label: Does not include any patient names, initials, or uniquely identifying information
Refers to patients by case number, room number, appointment time, or generic reference
Does not include specific diagnoses, treatments, or medical details that could identify a patient in context

rubric.name: Bounded Process Steps
rubric.description: Multi-step processes use numbered steps, capped at 5. If a process needs more than 5 steps to explain in email, it needs a training session — the email should announce the training, not attempt to replace it.

dimensions.label: Processes with more than two actions use numbered steps
No process in the email exceeds 5 numbered steps
If a process is too complex for 5 steps, the email schedules training instead of attempting full documentation

rubric_used.coaching_notes: James's non-negotiable: every new process has a fallback. In clinical settings, 'the system is down' is not an edge case, it's a Tuesday. Will reject any email that names a patient or introduces a process without explaining what to do when it breaks.

rounds.draft:
**To:** Front Desk Team
**From:** [Your Name]
**Subject:** New Tablet Check-In Process — Starting [Date]

---

Hi team,

Starting [Date], patients will complete their check-in forms on tablets rather than paper. From the patient's perspective, this looks like a small change: they'll be handed a tablet at the desk instead of a clipboard, and most will be ready to move to a room about **2–3 minutes faster** than with our current paper process. The waiting area flow should feel noticeably smoother during busy morning slots.

**How the new check-in process works:**

1. Hand the patient a sanitized tablet from the charging station and let them know they can complete their forms right at the desk or take a seat.
2. Once they submit, confirm their check-in is showing as complete in the system before they sit down.
3. Notify the clinical team via [your usual method] that the patient is ready.

**If the tablet system goes down or loses connectivity:**

Our building's Wi-Fi can be intermittent, so please keep a supply of paper backup forms in the top drawer of each front desk station at all times. If a tablet fails to load or submit within about 60 seconds:

1. Switch the patient to a paper form without explanation or delay — just say "Let me grab this for you instead."
2. Complete check-in manually and flag the paper form with a sticky note marked **"Manual — needs entry"** so the record can be updated later.
3. Set the tablet aside and let [designated contact] know after the patient is seated.

This shift moves us away from paper storage and reduces transcription time on the back end, which is part of our broader effort to streamline records handling.

If you have questions before the go-live date, please reach out to [Your Name] directly. A brief walkthrough will be scheduled for [Date/Time] — attendance is encouraged, especially if you'll be opening that week.

Thanks for your flexibility as we make this transition.

[Your Name]
[Title]
[Contact Information]

rounds.draft:
**To:** Front Desk Team
**From:** [Your Name]
**Subject:** New Tablet Check-In Process — Starting [Date]

---

Hi team,

Starting [Date], patients will complete their check-in forms on tablets rather than paper. Here's what changes for them: instead of a clipboard at the counter, they'll be handed a tablet and can complete their forms while seated. Based on our intake timing, this should save approximately **2 minutes per appointment** during the form-completion stage — which, across a full morning, means patients are reaching their rooms faster and the front desk area stays visibly clearer between arrivals. Rooms should be turning over more smoothly as a result.

The operational reason: eliminating paper forms reduces manual transcription time and removes the need for physical form storage, as part of our ongoing records streamlining effort.

**How the new check-in process works:**

1. Hand the patient a sanitized tablet from the charging station and let them know they're welcome to complete their forms at the desk or take a seat.
2. Once they submit, confirm their check-in appears as complete in the system before they move to the waiting area.
3. Notify the clinical team via [your usual method] that the patient is ready.

**If the tablet system goes down or loses connectivity:**

Given our building's intermittent Wi-Fi, please keep paper backup forms stocked in the top drawer of each front desk station at all times. If a tablet fails to load or submit within about 60 seconds:

1. Switch the patient to a paper form without delay — just say "Let me grab this for you instead."
2. Complete check-in manually and mark the form with a sticky note labeled **"Manual — needs entry"** so it can be entered into the system later.
3. Set the tablet aside and notify [designated contact] once the patient is seated.

**Mandatory walkthrough: [Date/Time], [Location]**

Please plan to attend. This is your opportunity for hands-on time with the tablets before go-live. If your schedule creates a conflict, contact [Your Name] directly — all front desk staff need to complete this before [go-live date].

Thanks,
[Your Name]
[Title]
[Contact Information]
